html:
SMTO-AUT-0006 — This account isn't allowed to run that command as administrator

GUID: 63816883-5650-455d-a1bc-623938585aff
Slug: privilege-not-permitted
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: aut

What happened

  • The computer's own rules don't let the account SMTO uses run this command with administrator rights, so the command did not run. Entering a different password won't change that.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages that computer to allow the Gateway's account to run only this specific command with administrator rights, if that's appropriate. The block comes from that computer's own permission rules, which SMTO can't change.
  2. Or, if another Gateway runs as an account that already has this permission, select it in the Gateway picker next to Add context before your next message. Each Gateway, the helper program that runs commands, uses its own account, so another one may already be allowed.
  3. Or ask SMTO in the conversation to find a way to do the task that doesn't need administrator rights. Many checks and reports work with normal rights, which avoids the blocked command entirely.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its step is marked Elevated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the exact command, to the person who manages that computer. Don't ask for the account to get full administrator rights for everything; only the needed command should be allowed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • sudo refused elevation for the selected Gateway account before the command started (its output matched a policy denial such as 'not in the sudoers' or 'not allowed to execute'), indicating a host sudoers rule blocks this account and command.

What this means

  • Before elevation is confirmed, the sudo-output classifier matched a host-policy denial indicator; this is evidence to inspect the account's sudo rules. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Before elevation is confirmed, the sudo-output classifier matched a host-policy denial indicator; this is evidence to inspect the account's sudo rules.

How to diagnose it

  • Have the host administrator compare the exact account and command with sudo policy and the retained authentication outcome.

How to fix it

  • On the target host, review the sudoers rules for the Gateway's execution account and this exact command (for example with sudo -l -U and the account name), and grant only the minimum rule required, or use an account or operation that is already permitted. A different password will not help; do not grant broad sudo rights.
  • Ask the host administrator to review the exact command and account against the intended sudo policy. Use an authorized account or a permitted operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended command is permitted by host policy and its authorized elevation is confirmed.

What not to do

  • Do not grant broad permissions; verify the exact resource, identity and required access.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
